title: Enemy and combat
intro: Four steps, one script that grows. The robot meets an enemy. Both sides get health and an attack power, written with type hints this time; then the attacks, the enemy's turn, and a fight that runs until one side falls. The stage shows both health bars and, after a fight, who won.

steps.title: Two sides, with types
steps.prompt: Both fighters need numbers, and this time each one says what kind of value it holds. Declare, at the top of the script, `health` and `max_health` as `int` starting at the number `100`, `attack_power` as `int` at the number `20`, then for the enemy `enemy_health` and `enemy_max_health` as `int` at the number `60` and `enemy_attack` as `int` at the number `15`. A type hint goes between the name and the value: `var health: int = 100`.
steps.starter:
# The robot and the enemy: health, the most health, and attack power for each.
# Declare all six member variables here, each with a type hint.
steps.solution:
var health: int = 100
var max_health: int = 100
var attack_power: int = 20
var enemy_health: int = 60
var enemy_max_health: int = 60
var enemy_attack: int = 15
hints: The shape is `var name: int = value`, with the colon right after the name.
Six lines, one per variable, all at the top of the script; the checks also look for the `: int` on each.

docs.name: var name: int = value
docs.what: declares a member variable that may only ever hold a whole number

docs.name: int
docs.what: the type of whole numbers; float is for decimals, String for text, bool for true or false

steps.title: Attack
steps.prompt: Write `attack`, which returns a `bool`: `func attack() -> bool:`. It takes `attack_power` away from `enemy_health`, keeps enemy_health from going below the number `0`, and returns `true` when the enemy has fallen, meaning enemy_health is `0`, otherwise `false`. Three hits of 20 bring a 60-health enemy to exactly 0; the third one returns true.
steps.starter:
var health: int = 100
var max_health: int = 100
var attack_power: int = 20
var enemy_health: int = 60
var enemy_max_health: int = 60
var enemy_attack: int = 15

# Write attack() -> bool below.
steps.solution:
var health: int = 100
var max_health: int = 100
var attack_power: int = 20
var enemy_health: int = 60
var enemy_max_health: int = 60
var enemy_attack: int = 15

func attack() -> bool:
	enemy_health -= attack_power
	if enemy_health < 0:
		enemy_health = 0
	return enemy_health == 0

tests.name: One attack leaves the enemy at 40
One attack does not fell it
A fourth attack keeps it at 0

hints: Take the damage first, guard against going below 0 with an `if`, then decide what to return.
`enemy_health == 0` is already a bool: it can be returned as it is.
`-> bool` after the brackets promises a true or false comes back; every path must return one.

docs.name: func name() -> bool:
docs.what: a function that promises to return true or false
true when both sides are the same value

steps.title: The enemy's turn
steps.prompt: The robot's `take_damage` from the health milestone is back. Write `is_alive`, returning a `bool`: `true` while `health` is above the number `0`. Then write `enemy_turn`, also returning a `bool`: it calls `take_damage(enemy_attack)` and returns what `is_alive()` gives. A turn takes 15; seven turns bring 100 health to 0, and that seventh turn returns false.
steps.starter:
var health: int = 100
var max_health: int = 100
var attack_power: int = 20
var enemy_health: int = 60
var enemy_max_health: int = 60
var enemy_attack: int = 15

func attack() -> bool:
	enemy_health -= attack_power
	if enemy_health < 0:
		enemy_health = 0
	return enemy_health == 0

func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:
	health -= amount
	if health < 0:
		health = 0

# Write is_alive() -> bool and enemy_turn() -> bool below.

tests.name: At full health the robot is alive
One enemy turn reports still alive
The seventh turn reports the fall

hints: `return health > 0` is the whole body of is_alive.
enemy_turn has two lines: the take_damage call, then `return is_alive()`.
Do not subtract in enemy_turn yourself; take_damage already does it and keeps health at 0 or above.

docs.what: true when the left side is bigger than the right

steps.title: Fight to the end
steps.prompt: Write `fight`, which returns a `String`: `func fight() -> String:`. It runs turns in a `while` loop as long as both sides stand. Each pass: call `attack()`, and if it returned `true`, return `"won"`; otherwise call `enemy_turn()`, and if that returned `false`, return `"lost"`. With the numbers so far the robot wins in three attacks and takes two hits on the way. A `spawn_enemy` function is given so the checks can bring in a tougher enemy.

tests.name: Winning costs two hits: 70 health left
A brute with 500 health and 40 power wins
An enemy with 40 health falls in two attacks, one hit taken

hints: The loop condition is `is_alive() and enemy_health > 0`; inside, the two ifs each `return` a word.
`if attack():` is enough: attack already gives true or false. `if not enemy_turn():` catches the fall.
A `return` after the loop, for safety, keeps the `-> String` promise on every path.

docs.name: while
docs.what: repeats the block while the condition is true; a return inside ends the function at once

docs.name: and / not
docs.what: and is true when both sides are; not flips true and false

docs.name: -> String
docs.what: a function that promises to return text

godot: Open Godot and make a new project called Robot Fight.
Create a 2D scene with a Node2D root named Arena, and attach a script to it.
Copy the whole script from step 4 into it, type hints and all; Godot's editor now warns you if a wrong kind of value is put in one of the variables.

Add two Label children, Robot and Enemy. Write `func show_bars():` that sets `$Robot.text = str(health) + " / " + str(max_health)` and the same for the enemy, and call it at the end of attack and take_damage.
In `func _ready():` call `print(fight())` and run the scene (F6): the Output panel says won and the labels show 70 and 0.
Change _ready to `spawn_enemy(500, 40)` before the fight and run again: lost, and the robot's label reads 0.
Add a Button node, connect its pressed signal to a function that calls `attack()` then `show_bars()`, and fight by clicking.
Try making attack_power a float and read the warning Godot gives where it is subtracted from an int.
